27.19.2.en: * "Want overtakes him like water, and the tempest stealeth him away in the night" [20]... It is not unfitting to liken want to water; for this reason the torments in hell are usually called the lake, which swallows up whoever is received into it and carries him down to the depths. Therefore it was said by the prophet in the person of mankind: [They have cut off my life in the dungeon (the pit)] (Lam 3:53). While the victorious who escape from it sing, saying: [O LORD my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me. O LORD, thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit] (Ps 2:30-3).

27.19.3.en: * "A tempest stealeth him away in the night" [20]. What is it that he calls "the night" here but the hidden time of the sudden departure?

27.20.0.en: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place [21].

27.20.1.en: The storm of wrath blows upon him like a violent and most terrible east wind, carrying him away as to eternal destruction. But upon the righteous man blows the breath of God's love and mercies, to carry him to the bosom of the Father in heaven! Death is destructive for the wicked man, and for the righteous most joyful.

27.20.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that the burning east wind is the evil spirit with his fiery darts, with which he stirs up the passions in the wicked man and brings him into the eternal hell.

27.20.3.en: * "The burning wind shall carry him away by force and drive him out" [21]. What is this that he calls here the burning wind but the evil spirit who stirs up the flame of various passions in the heart, and so drags him off to eternal punishment? It is said that the burning wind carries off the wicked by force, because the conspirator, the evil spirit, who inflames the man who lives in evil, draws him to the torments at death. By "the burning wind" he usually means the unclean spirit who, by the breath of evil suggestions, inflames the hearts of the wicked with earthly passions.

27.20.4.en: * "And as a whirlwind it hurleth him out of his place" [21]. The place of the wicked man is the enjoyment of temporal life and the pleasure of the flesh. Therefore each one is in a way carried from his place by a whirlwind when fear of the last day swallows him up, and he is separated from all his delights.

27.20.6.en: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare.

27.21.0.en: He would fain flee out of his hand [22].

27.21.1.en: While the wicked man was in the world, God had compassion on him, even in disciplining him very firmly, opening His doors to him that he might return to Him by repentance, but on the day of judgment he will not be able to flee from the divine justice. Now is the time of mercy and longsuffering.

27.22.0.en: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place [23].

27.22.1.en: After Job spoke of the temporary prosperity of the wicked man, and pictured for us the bitterness of his soul as he faces death, he now sees how the weak and some sinners find in this a practical lesson from the bitter fruit of evil, and so they clap their hands in amazement, and turn back from their evil way, and seek life with God.

27.22.2.en: "Men shall clap their hands at him," that is, they rejoice at the punishment that puts an end to injustice, and brings the devil and his hosts down to hell. "When the wicked perish, there is shouting" (Prov 11:10); [in the very place where he lived in luxury the righteous shall laugh at him] (Ps 52:6), [they shall be ashes under the soles of the feet of the godly] (Mal 4:3).

27.22.3.en: * When the sinner dies, those who witness his death shut their mouths while they hiss (like the sound of a serpent), and so they turn to those spiritual words which they had made light of, and so they begin to believe, and learn what they had not believed before, when they supposed that the wicked man lived in prosperity. Solomon says: [When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise] (Prov 11:21)

27.22.4.en: * Every stroke from God is either to cleanse the present life in us, or as the beginning of a punishment to come... But as for the persons for whom the strokes are a curse and not a chastening, it is said of them: [Thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction] (Jer 3:5). For these their strokes begin in this life, and continue in eternal strokes. The Lord says by Moses: [For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell] (Deut 22:32).

27.22.6.en: Who supports me in my trials but You?

27.22.7.en: * You alone are the Almighty, and You became tempted that You might help me.

27.22.8.en: Grant me wisdom when a trial of false accusations comes upon me.

27.22.9.en: And grant me patience when a bitter affliction comes upon me!

27.22.10.en: I believe that You are living, caring for all my affairs!

27.22.11.en: You permit bitterness to come to me, and You turn my bitterness into sweetness.

27.22.12.en: * Let affliction be for my spiritual growth.

27.22.13.en: So that my tongue may not rush into an unseemly word, nor my thoughts fall into ingratitude.

27.22.14.en: Let me not flatter the wicked at the cost of the purity of my heart, but act with a good conscience in all things!

27.22.15.en: For my death is lighter than my flattering of the wicked!

27.22.16.en: * Take away from me all evil, for it is deadly to my soul.

27.22.17.en: Take away from me all hypocrisy, for it deceives me.

27.22.18.en: * Teach me how to enter my closet and speak with You, O heavenly Father.

27.22.19.en: I have nothing greater than to possess You!

27.22.20.en: * You are the Guide, leading me to the way of salvation.

27.22.21.en: You are the Tutor, bearing me and training me by Your grace.

27.22.22.en: You are the Teacher, giving me Yourself, O divine Wisdom!

27.22.23.en: * Why should I fear the wicked man?

27.22.24.en: Even if he prospers, it is for a time; eternal punishment awaits him.

27.22.25.en: If his children are many, they suffer even from hunger.

27.22.26.en: His offspring become a burden on society, and at their death no one honors them; even their widows do not grieve for them.

27.22.27.en: And if they grow rich in silver and garments,

27.22.28.en: what use is silver to them without the pure silver word of God?

27.22.29.en: And what use are garments to them unless they are covered by the blood of Christ?

27.22.30.en: They build palaces to perpetuate their memory, and these are like an old garment that the moth has reached.

27.22.31.en: They gather wealth, and in a moment their souls are required of them.

27.22.32.en: The tempest of death blows upon them as in the midst of the darkness of night; their eyes are opened to see the lake blazing with fire before them.

27.22.33.en: The enemy of good draws them to dwell with him eternally.

28.0.0.en: 1 "Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it. 2 Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone. 3 He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death. 4 He hath dug a mine far from the inhabitants; without a foothold, hanging far from men, they dangle. 5 As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire. 6 The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold."

28.0.1.en: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it [1].

28.0.2.en: Men strive to know the secrets of nature, such as discovering precious metals, gold and silver, and they have been able to. For the sake of wealth man strives in these things and the like, yet in his folly he does not care to become acquainted with the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven. For temporal wealth and curiosity he searches for what is buried in the earth, and does not search for the salvation of his soul and his eternal glory.

28.0.3.en: * "For there is a place from which silver comes, and a place for gold where they fine it; iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten like stone" [cf. 1-2 LXX]. By this he means that if God has set an order for general matters, how much more does He set an order concerning human affairs... He foresees things beforehand and cares for them Himself, and nothing happens by chance. Or rather he means that the gathering of (natural) facts is a matter clearly visible, while the plan of God Himself is invisible. Silver and brass have their known place, but the place of wisdom no one knows, but God alone knows it. (God) says to man: [The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom](a), and to depart from evil is understanding.

28.0.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * As silver is often refined, so the righteous man is tried, and becomes the Lord's coin, receiving the royal image. Solomon also calls [the tongue of the just choice silver, refined with fire] (cf. Prov 20:10), showing that the teaching which is tested and its wisdom proved is praised and accepted, where it is refined on earth when the soul of the Gnostic (the spiritual man possessing knowledge) is sanctified in various ways, withdrawing from earthly fires. As for the body in which (this soul) dwells, it is purified and gains the purity fitting for a holy temple.

28.0.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria Pope Gregory (the Great) offers us a symbolic interpretation of this phrase: if man searches for silver and gold to extract them from the stones, it is fitting for the preachers to work without ceasing that they may have spiritual silver, that is, the word of God purified seven times in the fire like silver (Ps 12:6). And that they may have gold, which signifies the splendid, wise, heavenly life.

28.0.6.en: And the Pope distinguishes between the sincere preaching that presents pure silver and gold from the Holy Scriptures, interpreting them according to the mind of the Fathers, as the early Church lived them, and the heretics. For the latter do not present silver and gold refined by fire, but teachings of their own, for their own honor and for their human glory.

28.0.7.en: * "Silver has its beginning in veins (in the stones), and gold has a place where they fine it" [1]. Silver signifies the power of speech, and gold the splendor of life or the splendor of wisdom... It is as though he says plainly: he who prepares himself for words of sincere preaching must draw the sources of his presentation (of subjects) from the Holy Scriptures, and so base everything he utters on a divine foundation, for the benefit of those to whom he speaks.

28.0.8.en: Heretics often seek, in support of the false things they present out of their own heads, to extract things that certainly have no support from the pages of the Holy Scriptures.

28.0.9.en: For this reason the great preacher counsels his disciple, saying: "O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called" (1 Tim 20:6). For the heretics, longing to be glorified as though they were skilled in thought, present new things that did not occur in the ancient books of the ancient Fathers, and so they cast the seeds of ignorance to the wretched who listen to them, desiring to appear wise.

28.0.10.en: It is as though he says plainly: The true wisdom of the believers has a place in the catholic Church, and it suffers troubles that come from you and from your persecution of it, but it is purified from every impurity of sins by the fire of your persecution. So it is written: [Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity] (Sir 2:5)...

28.0.11.en: The Apostle Paul teaches us when he says: "Though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing" (1 Cor 3:13). For some have wrong thoughts about God, and others have right thoughts about the Creator, but do not keep unity with their brethren. The former are cut off because of their error in the faith, and the latter because of their schism. For this reason the first part of the Ten Commandments forbade the sin of both parties, for it was said with the divine voice: [Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might]. And at once he added [Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself] (Deut 5:6; Mk 30:12-31). For he who believes what is wrong concerning God certainly does not love God, and he who has right conceptions of God and rends the unity of the Holy Church obviously does not love his neighbor, since he refuses to take him as his companion.

28.0.13.en: * The words of the Lord are pure words (Ps 12:6)... He says "pure," without the dross of false appearance. For many preach the truth in impurity, selling it in order to receive a bribe for temporal gain.

28.0.14.en: St. Augustine * (Schism) is the weapon of Satan, turning everything upside down. As long as the body is united together Satan cannot find an entrance, but the stumbling comes because of division. Where does schism come from? From opinions contrary to the teachings of the Apostles. And where do these opinions come from? From men's slavery to the belly and other passions... This is what he said when he wrote to the Philippians: "Whose God is their belly" (Phil 3:19).

28.0.15.en: St. John Chrysostom It is fitting for the preacher of the truth, indeed for every believer, to present silver and gold from God, that is, His surpassing heavenly peace, not the peace of this passing world; he presents God the Savior, who is the true peace.

28.0.16.en: * Peace will be your gold; peace is your silver; peace is your land. Peace is your life, your God is peace. You will have peace in everything you desire!

28.1.0.en: St. Augustine Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone [2].

28.1.1.en: Although the extraction of silver and gold requires greater effort than the extraction of iron and brass, the latter two metals are more useful to man, and because of their abundance their price is much lower than that of silver and gold. A man can live without silver and gold, though with great difficulty, but at present it is impossible for him to live without iron and brass. It is the surpassing wisdom of God that made what is necessary for man more abundant and its extraction easier, while what is for luxury is less in quantity and harder to extract.

28.1.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that the extraction of all these metals, silver and gold and iron and brass, from dust and stones is a sign of the holy men of God (despite the difference in their spiritual level and their role in the work of preaching and witness for God), but all are extracted from dust and stones. We were dust and stones, occupied with temporal things, hard of heart. But the grace of God raised up from us people who are witnesses for God, who enjoy fellowship in the divine nature, in love and tenderness and meekness and humility and purity and holiness, and so on. All these are not from ourselves, but are the free gifts of God to believers who earnestly seek the salvation of their own souls and the salvation of their brethren in humanity.

28.1.3.en: * "Iron is taken out of the earth" [2]. It is as though he says plainly: Men of strength whose tongues are sharper than swords have become iron in this violent battle in defense of the faith, those who were at one time "earth," in the sphere of low works. When a man sins, it is said to him: [Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return](b). But [iron is taken out of the earth] when the stern warrior of the Church is separated from earthly conduct...

28.1.4.en: Was he not taken out even of the earth, who, occupied with earthly matters, served in the collecting of tribute (like Zacchaeus the tax collector)? But being taken out of the earth, he was strengthened with the strength of iron, the Lord bound him to the Gospel, tearing the hearts of unbelievers with his tongue as with a sharp sword. He who was formerly weak and entangled in earthly works afterward became strong in heavenly preaching.

28.1.5.en: "And the stone is molten by heat, and becomes brass." The stone dissolves by heat when the hard and cold heart is touched by the fire of divine love and is poured out in the blazing fire of the Spirit. Then it has a life glowing with heat in work. To the extent that it was hard before in its love of the world, it becomes strong in its love of God.

28.1.7.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus holds that the mind of the devout believer is like iron extracted from flint or stones.

28.1.8.en: * They are like iron extracted from flint, radiating fire from the fertile gold fit for light, for a small spark can quickly form the flame of truth within.

28.1.9.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus When St. Cyril of Jerusalem speaks of the resurrection of the body he says that it becomes like iron heated by fire. It is the same body that we have in this life, but with a fiery nature fitting for eternity.

28.1.10.en: * This was recorded specially, how Paul says plainly: "For this corruptible must put on incorruption" (1 Cor 15:53). So this body will rise and put on incorruption and be fashioned anew. And as iron mingles with fire and becomes fire, or rather as the Lord who raises us knows: this body will rise, but it will not remain as it is now.

28.1.11.en: It is an eternal body. It needs no nourishment for its life as it does now, nor steps for its ascent, for it will be spiritual. It is a wonderful matter that we are not worthy to speak of, for it is said in the Gospel of St. Matthew the Evangelist: "Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father" (Mt 13:43), [and as the moon and as the brightness of the firmament] (Dan 12:3).

28.1.12.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection.

28.2.0.en: The stones of darkness, and the shadow of death [3].

28.2.1.en: When Job speaks of extracting metals from the belly of the earth, that is, from the dark mines, man in order to obtain them enters the mines to examine what is in them, using torches to set an end to the darkness so that it does not hinder him from determining his goal. He risks his life, and enters the rough places in order to extract the metals.

28.2.2.en: He who has no knowledge of the art of mining mocks those who search for the metals. He looks at them as people who expose themselves to dangers and death without purpose. So God extracts from our dust and stones metals precious in His eyes. But many are ignorant of God's plan and reckon Him as one who enters into darkness and examines things of no value. In other words, it is fitting for us to trust in God's plan and His providence and His work for us. He offers us salvation, whatever its cost, for in His foreknowledge He sees the glories we shall enjoy. He sees us as gold and silver and brass and iron extracted from earth and stones! He extracts from us, who were darkness, light. And as the Apostle says: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord" (Eph 5:8).

28.2.3.en: * He says "He hath set a place for the darkness" [3] as if to say that the mind also has a place, for the darkness knows how to retrace its steps and efface itself (before the break of day)... He urges us not to demand an accounting (from God). He says: "Why is there darkness? Do you not know God to be the Almighty, who does everything with wisdom?"

28.2.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * [He hath set a time for the darkness, and He Himself searcheth out all things, and every one] [3]. He Himself has set a time for the darkness, that is, He has set an end to the wicked, where they cease to be wicked. Thus it is said to them by the Apostle: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord" (Eph 8:5). The same great Apostle says to other disciples: "The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day" (Rom 12:13-13). For this reason it is said in the Song of Songs concerning the coming of the Church: "Who is she that looketh forth as the morning?" (Song 10:6). The Church is likened to the morning, that is, to the knowledge of the faith, turning from the darkness of sins to the splendor of the light of righteousness...

28.2.5.en: Since God does what is good, and carries out the dispensation, and does not do evil, He controls the things that the wicked do so that matters do not go on to what is bad, but He searches out the end of all things and the end of every one, and bears all things in longsuffering, and sees the end of the elect, for evil turns to good for them...

28.2.6.en: God saw the end to which Saul would come even while he was persecuting (the Church); He sees him fall to the ground and say: "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?" (Acts 6:9)...

28.2.7.en: He saw the people of Nineveh disobeying, but He looked to the end of their disobedience in their practicing reform (repentance).

28.2.8.en: He also saw the end of disobedient Sodom, and looked to the end of the burning of lust in the fire of hell.

28.2.9.en: He saw the end of the world of the Gentiles, while it was occupied in the darkness of evils, how one day it would shine with the light of faith.

28.2.11.en: God the Creator, wonderful in His works, created the earth and brought forth upon it the creeping things and the beasts, and also created man from its dust. He still (creates) a new nature fitting for eternal life.

28.2.12.en: * From one earth come forth creeping things and beasts of prey and the flock, and upon it trees are set, and foods are found, and gold and silver and brass and iron and stone!

28.2.13.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem He hath dug a mine far from the inhabitants.

28.3.0.en: Hanging far from men, they dangle [4].

28.3.1.en: The text appears in the writings of Pope Gregory (the Great) as "the stone of darkness also, and the shadow of the (sweeping) valley, is divided from the people on a journey."

28.3.2.en: When some dig in rocky ground uninhabited by people, others hear of them or see them doing so, and mock them. They suppose that they want to draw water from within the earth, but why do they choose stony regions far from the inhabited places? They are like those who dangle their feet in a pit of no use. So some mock God's plan and His saving work, just as the Jews mocked the Apostles and disciples who went out to preach among the pagan nations, like those who dig mines in a rocky, waterless land, without aim or hope!

28.3.3.en: * "The stone of darkness also, and the shadow of the (sweeping) valley, is divided from the people on a journey" [3-4]. What was that Jewish people, hardened in unbelief, who refused to receive the faith that had been announced to them beforehand through the prophecies by the Giver of life, but the stone of darkness? This is brought about by the hardness of their violence and their wrapping themselves in unbelief....

28.3.4.en: Perhaps by the sweeping torrent he points to being watered by the holy preaching, as it was said by Solomon: [The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley (the torrent) shall pick it out] (Prov 17:30). For the wicked, finding fault with God's judgments, mock their father, and heretics of every kind, who despise the preaching of the Holy Church and scoff at its fruit, are they not despisers of the pain of their mother? It is not unseemly to call her their mother also, for those who speak against her came out of her, as John testifies, saying: "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us" (1 Jn 19:2). But "the ravens of the valley" come when the true preachers go forth to defend the Holy Church from the streams of the Holy Scriptures.

28.4.0.en: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire [5].

28.4.1.en: Some hold that the earth that brings forth wheat for us to eat also brings forth fuel (petroleum) for the fire to feed on. By the wisdom given to us by the Creator we find what satisfies us from the very earth from which we bring out what we use as fuel.

28.4.2.en: Others hold that Job points to Sodom and Gomorrah, the land marked as exceedingly fertile, producing wheat in abundance on which many fed, which was turned because of the wickedness of its inhabitants into a furnace of fire, as God sent down upon it fire and brimstone.

28.4.3.en: Still others hold that in speaking of man's concern to extract precious metals from mines under the earth, he means that they turned the earth that overflows to them with food into mines, in which many perish because of the dangers to which they are exposed, so that it became like a furnace of fire under the earth.

28.4.4.en: * Pope Gregory (the Great) sees here a prophecy about Judaism, which at the coming of the Lord ought to have borne witness to Him and preached, presenting to the world Christ the bread of life, but through the envy of the Jewish leaders it was turned into a hidden fire destroying souls. [The earth, out of it cometh bread, is turned up in its place as it were fire] [5]. What occupied Judaism was to give bread, for it was accustomed to set out the words of the Law before the people. The sons of perdition were no longer able to interpret this very Law, as the prophet Jeremiah laments in his Lamentations, saying: "The young children ask bread, and no man breaketh it unto them" (Lam 4:4). But this [earth is turned up in its place as it were fire], for it destroys itself with the coal of envy when it sees the miracles of the believers... Was it not inflamed with the flame of the coals of its envy when it saw the miracles of our Savior, so that some of its men said: "What do we? for this man doeth many miracles" (Jn 47:11)? Or "Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him" (Jn 19:12)

28.5.0.en: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold [6].

28.5.1.en: It was fitting for the men of Judaism or its religious leaders to present Christ the bread of life, and so become living stones in the temple of the Lord, of sapphire, that is, bearing the heavenly mark, so that the dust is turned to gold, in that the earthly are turned into the heavenly, if one may say so.

28.5.2.en: Some hold that God in His surpassing wisdom made many precious things, such as silver and gold and petroleum, hidden under the earth, or in the stones, so that man would not fix his eyes on these things, but lift his eyes to heaven. He treads them under foot, making light of them, so that his whole heart may be fastened to God.

28.5.3.en: The sapphire is counted in value next to the diamond, and is one of the most precious gems; it may be red, blue or yellow, but it is most often blue in color.

28.5.4.en: * "The stones of it are the place of sapphires, and it hath dust of gold" [6]. To the declaration of the glory mentioned before is added the iniquity of the sin that follows it. For the fall of each one is a wicked, criminal deed, since before the fall he was able to attain to a greater height... The stones signify the minds of the strong, when Peter said to the saints: "As lively stones, a spiritual house, an holy priesthood" (1 Pet 5:2). And the Lord promises the Church this when she comes, saying by the prophet: [Behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones. And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD] (Isa 11:54-13). For He sets stones in her in order, distinguishing the holy souls in her according to the difference of their merits. "He lays her foundations with sapphires," for these stones bear in themselves the likeness of the color of heaven, and so the strength of the Church is founded in the souls that seek heavenly things...

28.5.5.en: And because she shines through faith in the splendor of the surpassing life and wisdom, there was added: "dust of gold"... But this gold was afterward dimmed by the darkness of unbelief. The prophet Jeremiah lamented its blackness, saying: "How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed!" (Lam 1:4) For the gold became dim, and the ancient splendor of faith and innocence itself grew dark with the night of evil, as unbelief came upon them.

28.6.0.en: 7 "There is a path which no bird of prey knoweth, and which the falcon's eye hath not seen: 8 The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the visitor passed by it. 9 He putteth forth his hand upon the flint; he overturneth the mountains by the roots. 10 He cutteth out a tunnel among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing. 11 He restraineth the trickling of the rivers, and the things that are hid bringeth he forth to light."

28.6.1.en: There is a path which no bird of prey knoweth, and which the falcon's eye hath not seen [7].

28.6.2.en: Though it is within man's power to exploit the earth, so that it yields wheat and crops for his food, and to extract from its belly and from its rocks silver and gold and petroleum and precious stones, there is another wisdom that is not given except to him who seeks it, namely the possibility of knowing the divine mysteries, especially the mystery of the divine Incarnation and the mystery of salvation. However sharp a sight man may enjoy, like the sight of eagles and other birds of keen vision, he will not be able to see divine things by himself.

28.6.3.en: He chose birds of prey, because they fly to very great distances in search of food, and can see their prey from a great height, swoop down upon it and then return to their nest without losing the way, or mistaking it, even if it resembles their own nest.

28.6.4.en: The Chaldean Targum gives as an interpretation of this phrase that Satan, flying like a bird, did not see the tree of life nor recognize it, and neither did the eyes of Eve look upon it, nor did the sons of men walk toward it, nor did the serpent turn toward it.

28.6.5.en: Some hold that one who is concerned with extracting metals has eyes surpassing those of the eagle, with which he looks to great distances under the earth, and so knows the places of the precious metals, and digs and extracts them.

28.6.6.en: For the sake of riches and the acquiring of wealth it is not hard for man to penetrate the layers of the earth by the craft of mining to obtain an abundance of precious metals. And for the desire for food it is not hard for the ravening lions to recognize the paths among the forests and the wilds to hunt prey for themselves and their young; nor is prey hidden from the sight of birds of prey at lofty distances, yet the mysteries of divine wisdom remain hidden from man without the surpassing grace of God.

28.6.7.en: Human wisdom is a natural gift that God gives to man in degrees fitting for each one, as a talent by which one person is distinguished from another, but divine wisdom is a gift offered to him who seeks it sincerely and desires it.

28.6.8.en: * The wisdom of this world is not the wisdom of God. The wisdom of God is real, and nothing that corrupts it touches it. The wisdom of the world is foolish, though the simplicity of God's wisdom makes whoever receives it seem foolish in the eyes of the world. Believers receive this divine wisdom, and so are counted fools by the world.

28.6.9.en: Origen * Paul says that the wisdom of God is taught in harmony with the Lord, which shows that true wisdom is given through the Son.

28.7.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the visitor passed by it (nor has the lion walked in it) [8].

28.7.1.en: The young lion or lion's whelp walks among the forests and wilds as king of the beasts. It is as though he knows all the hidden paths, and no animal can hide from him. When he is hungry he knows how to reach his prey, as though he were acquainted with all the secrets of the region. So he who works in mining penetrates paths that he makes under the earth, which no lion's whelp has trodden, nor any lion walked in. And he who wishes to acquire the wisdom of God [the surpassing mystery of Christ] walks by the Holy Spirit a unique path that no creature can reach by himself, even if he be a great king possessing authority and surpassing strength and power!

28.7.2.en: Our Christ is the way, for as we walk in Him we become like spiritual lions, kings and priests unto God His Father (Rom 1:6).

28.7.3.en: * Paul enumerates two or three kinds of wisdom (1 Cor 1:20-25). First there is the wisdom which the world calls foolishness, and it is a greater wisdom than the other two. There is also the wisdom granted to men, by which we reason and act, and by which we advance and invent, and by which we know God. Finally there is a third kind of wisdom, in which there is contemplation of creation. The wisdom which the world counts foolishness is given to us through the Savior, so that the people who know God by natural wisdom and who are led to Him by contemplating the order of creation can receive salvation, which cannot be obtained by the two former kinds of wisdom, for they cannot rescue them from error.

28.7.4.en: Father Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus * The teaching of the Savior is sufficient in itself, without need of additional help, for He is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

28.7.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria He putteth forth his hand upon the flint.

28.8.0.en: He overturneth the mountains by the roots [9].

28.8.1.en: When Job speaks of the surpassing mystery of Christ, as the wisdom of God, he saw a wonder. He saw the Lord Christ, in His love, power and wisdom, stretch out His hand on the Cross to embrace the Gentiles who had become like hard flint, and raise up from the stones children to Abraham, or children of faith. The roots of the lofty mountains, that is, those who hold temporal authority, do not stand before Him.

28.8.2.en: By the simplicity of the Cross, the wisdom of God, which the pagan world counts foolishness and the Jews count a stumblingblock, the Lord caught the philosophers and those in authority. And as the Apostle Paul says: "God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; and base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are" (1 Cor 1:27-28).

28.8.3.en: * The philosophers could not accomplish what a few unlettered men accomplished, namely the conversion of the whole world. The philosophers spoke of trifles and persuaded only a very few. And the Apostles spoke of God and righteousness and judgment and converted great numbers.

28.8.4.en: * In human terms it is impossible for fishermen to catch philosophers, but this is what happened by the power of God's grace.

28.8.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * "He putteth forth his hand upon the flint, He overturneth the mountains by the roots" [9]. He puts forth his hand upon the flint, as He stretches out the arm of His preaching to the hardness of the Gentiles. So the blessed Job himself felt beforehand, presenting the history of the Gentiles, that they would know Him, and says: [Oh that they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!] (Job 24:19).

28.8.6.en: But what do we understand here by the mountains but those in authority in this world, who are puffed up in greatness because of their earthly standing? The psalmist says of them: "Touch the mountains, and they shall smoke" (Ps 5:144).

28.8.7.en: The roots of the mountains are their thoughts deep in pride. The mountains fall from their roots, because the worship of God brings the rulers of the world down to the earth, shattering their base thoughts.

28.8.9.en: * The Song lifts the bride to the highest summit of glory, bestowing on her the name of a fountain of living waters flowing from Lebanon. We have learned from Holy Scripture of the life-giving nature of God as a prophecy from the person of God saying: "They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters" (Jer 13:2). Then the Lord Christ says to the Samaritan woman: "Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water" (Jn 10:4). Then He said: "If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive)" (Jn 37:7-39).

28.8.10.en: Each of these passages says that the living water is the holy nature, so the Song may rightly call the bride truly a well of living waters flowing from Lebanon. This is in fact contrary to what is known, for wells usually contain still water, whereas the bride has running water in a deep well, and her waters flow continually.

28.8.11.en: Who is able and worthy to understand the wonders granted to the bride? It is clear that she has reached the utmost of her hopes, for she has been compared with the eternal Beauty from which all beauty arose. And in her spring she is exactly like the spring of her Bridegroom, her life like His life, her water like His water. His word is living, and by it every soul that receives Him lives.

28.8.12.en: These waters flow from God, as the fountain of living waters says: "For I proceeded forth and came from God" (Jn 42:8).

28.8.13.en: The bride keeps the overflow of His living water in the well of her soul, and becomes a house that treasures these living waters that flow from Lebanon, that is, that form streams from Lebanon, as the text says.

28.8.14.en: We have come into fellowship with God by possessing this well, so that we may fulfil the commandment of Wisdom (Proverbs 17:5, 18), and drink waters from our own well, and not from another's well. We enjoy this in Christ our Lord, to whom be glory and majesty forever, Amen.

28.9.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa He cutteth out a tunnel among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing [10].

28.9.1.en: Job stands amazed at the power of the Savior and His love, for it is He who grants that in man, who has become like a rock, springs of living water burst forth within him, and at the same time looks upon man not with contempt, nor to condemn him for his heart of stone, but as His own living icon, most precious in His eyes. He removes from man the hardness of his heart of stone, and raises from him a heart full of love.

28.9.2.en: Some hold that in the craft of mining they cut channels for water in the rocks, and so the veins of metals which they are extracting are revealed to them.

28.9.3.en: * "He cutteth out channels (waters) among the rocks." He cuts rivers of preaching in the hard hearts of the Gentiles.

28.9.4.en: In the same way the prophet speaks of the watering of the wildernesses of the Gentiles: [He turneth the wilderness into a standing water, and dry ground into watersprings] (Ps 35:107). Likewise the Lord promises in the Gospel: "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water" (Jn 38:7). What we heard as a promise has now been fulfilled.

28.9.5.en: Do you not see how the holy preachers overflowed like a spring from Judaism through the catholic Church spread over the whole world as channels of the heavenly commandments, flowing abundantly from the mouths of the Gentiles. This is because He has cut channels in the rocks; He has made the river of holy preaching flow from hard hearts.

28.9.6.en: "And his eye seeth every precious thing" [10]. It is a matter that must especially be kept in mind, that each individual soul is counted all the more precious in God's sight, the more it despises itself out of its love of the truth. "When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel?" (1 Sam 17:15)... And on the contrary, he who counts himself most precious becomes very small with God... [He beholdeth the humble, but the proud he knoweth afar off] (Ps 6:138). Therefore [his eye seeth every precious thing]. In Holy Scripture the expression "God sees" is used in place of "God chooses," as in the Gospel: "for He chooses the humble. God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty" (1 Cor 27:1). He "saw what was precious" when He visited the human soul as it held itself in contempt, enjoying the enlightenment of His grace. It is said of this soul by the prophet: [If thou take forth the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth] (Jer 19:15). For the present world is vile in God's sight, but the soul of man is precious to Him. He who separates the precious from the vile is called "as the mouth of God," for God gives His words to this man.

28.9.8.en: * The Holy Spirit is the river that flows, according to the Hebrews, from Christ to the lands. And we have received this as the mouth of Isaiah prophesied (Isa 12:66). This great river flows continually and will not cease; it is not only a river but also one of the abundant streams that overflow with greatness, as David said: [There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God] (Ps 4:46). For that city, the heavenly Jerusalem, is not watered by a canal, that is, an earthly river, but by that Holy Spirit who proceeds from the source of life. The stream that issues from Him who satisfies us seems to flow abundantly among the heavenly thrones and dominions and powers and angels and archangels, running in the fullest portion of the virtues of the seven-fold Spirit.

28.9.9.en: St. Ambrose * By the belly here (Jn 7:38) he means the heart... Where in Holy Scripture is it found that rivers of living water flow from his belly? It is not found.

28.9.10.en: What then does it mean: "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said"? Here we must pause, for the saying "out of his belly shall flow rivers" may be an affirmation that it is about Christ. For many said: "This is the Christ," and "When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles?" He shows the need for right knowledge, and that they be convinced not by miracles but by the Scripture...

28.9.11.en: He had said before: "Search the scriptures" (Jn 5:39) and also: "It is written in the prophets," [And they shall be all taught of God] (Jn 6:45), [there is one that accuseth you, even Moses] (Jn 5:45), and here he says: "As the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers," hinting at the greatness of grace and its overflow... And elsewhere he called it "eternal life," but here he calls it "rivers of water"...

28.9.12.en: For the grace of the Spirit, when it enters the mind and dwells, overflows more than any spring.

28.9.13.en: It will not cease and will not run dry...

28.9.14.en: In order to mean that it offers inexhaustible help, and at the same time an energy that does not fail, He called it a "well" and rivers, not one river, but countless rivers.

28.9.15.en: A person can clearly grasp what it means if he considers the wisdom of Stephen and the tongue of Peter and the zeal of Paul.

28.9.16.en: St. John Chrysostom * Which of the earthly beings was created in the image of God but man?

28.9.17.en: And to whom was given authority over all nature and its creatures, to make them his own?

28.9.18.en: It is an original honor that crowns his brow and lifts him up to heaven, above the stars, higher than the sun in loftiness and dignity... And though he is lower in rank than the angels because of his bond with a material body, he was given power to understand and know his Lord and Creator.

28.10.0.en: St. Basil the Great He restraineth the trickling of the rivers, and the things that are hid bringeth he forth to light [11].

28.10.1.en: A poetic expression of God's care for man, for when man cuts channels for water among the rocks to carry on mining, God preserves man's life and does not allow these channels to seep, so that the wall or roof of the mine would fall, and He supports man in his knowledge of the metals hidden in the mines under the earth.

28.10.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) offers a symbolic interpretation of this phrase, seeing in these rivers the overflow of the teachings of the early Fathers.

28.10.3.en: * "He searcheth the depths of the flood, and the things that are hid bringeth he forth to light" [11]. What are those called a flood but the sayings of the ancient Fathers? Who can estimate the mighty overflow that issued from the breast of Moses himself when he delivered the Law? What great overflow issued from the heart of David? What streams of water flowed from the lips of Solomon and the lips of all the prophets?
